text:
A: Hiya! Oh, hello, can you hear me? I'm Kerry.
B: Yes, I can hear you. I'm Nusrat.
A: Nusrat, lovely. Sorry, am I saying that right?
B: Yes, that's right.
A: Oh good. I'm in Chatham, in Kent. Where are you?
B: Ilford. East London.
A: Oh, not far then, sort of. Erm, how've you found it so far? I'm on my third one now, I think I'm getting the hang of it.
B: It's fine. Three minutes is short, so you can't really go into anything.
A: No, true, it goes so quick. So what d'you do? I'm guessing something clever, with all them binders behind you.
B: I'm a management accountant. I work for a housing association in Stratford. I do the monthly budget reports for the repairs division, so I look at what they planned to spend against what they actually spent, and I chase people when their numbers don't make sense.
A: Oh, wow. See, that's me out. I own half a hair salon, and the money side is the bit that keeps me up at night, honestly. I'm better with the people than the spreadsheets, d'you know what I mean?
B: What do you use for the accounts?
A: Erm, sorry?
B: For the bookkeeping. Software, or a spreadsheet?
A: Oh, erm, a bit of both, to be fair. I did a little course at adult education when we took it on. And my partner does some of it. But mostly it's a notebook and me doing sums in my head at two in the morning.
B: That's the problem, though. If it's in your head, it keeps you awake. If it's written down properly, you can look at it once a week and then stop.
A: Yeah. Yeah, that's fair, actually.
B: Do you know your monthly fixed costs? Rent, wages, utilities?
A: Roughly. The colour's the thing, the wholesaler's put the prices up again, that's the second time this year.
B: Then you track that separately. Product cost per client. If it keeps going up and your prices don't, that's where January comes from.
A: Oh my God, that's exactly it, January's always the worst. Sorry, you're doing a free consultation here, I should be paying you. I'd do your hair for it.
B: No, it's fine. I like this kind of thing more than small talk, to be honest.
A: Ha, no, I can tell, you're very straight to the point. I like it though, my mum's like that. Erm, what do you do when you're not working? Have you got kids?
B: One son, he's six. Year One. So most evenings it's dinner, homework, bed. Then I watch a drama or read.
A: Oh, what d'you read?
B: Crime novels, mostly. On the Kindle.
A: Oh, I love anything with a murder in it, but on the telly, Sunday nights. I'm not really a reader, I fall asleep after two pages.
B: Some of them are better on television anyway.
A: See, I'll take that. That makes me feel better. So is Ilford nice? I've only been through it on the train.
B: It's convenient. The Elizabeth line has made my commute much easier. Twenty minutes to Stratford now.
A: Oh, that's handy. It takes me twenty minutes to find a parking space on my road, the parking's a nightmare...
B: You should probably write down that product cost first, though.
A: Ha! Right, yes, I'm writing it down, look, I'm getting a pen. Product cost per...
